audit: Independent reconciliation of current UI-system evidence
scope: Local independent UI/UX design-system repository only; no consumer Micro app, repository, external URL, or real user was accessed.

severityPolicy.High: Directly reproduced behavior with a material interface consequence in a documented component contract.
severityPolicy.Moderate: Meaningful visual, reusable-contract, or cross-family governance issue supported by source/render evidence; not automatically a production emergency.
severityPolicy.Low: Preview, fixture, optional quality, or delivery/governance improvement with bounded current impact.
severityPolicy.rawSeverity: Each source track's original severity is retained in rawMetadata; skill-house-rule P0/P1 is not reinterpreted as application outage priority.

duplicateSourceIDsMerged.reason: Both report on the same temporary .brand-mark text glyph and converge on one owner decision/action: use or omit the approved symbol/lockup in preview chrome, rather than preserve an undocumented low-contrast letter.

findings.title_ar: طبقات التوكنز الدلالية غير مفصولة
findings.recommendationAr: أضف aliases دلالية تدريجيًا فوق CSS الحالي، ولا تبدأ DTCG بلا هدف إخراج ثانٍ.

rawMetadata.note: Severity normalized down: flat CSS is a confirmed architecture characteristic, not measured evidence of a wrong palette or current visual failure.

findings.evidence: One CSS :root layer combines brand, surface, text, feedback and scale values. Color, spacing, radius, type, shadows and motion variables exist; no primitive→semantic→component alias model or shared border-width, opacity, layer-role and responsive-threshold vocabulary was found. This is a maintainability/transfer finding, not proof that the light palette looks wrong. No screenshot defect is claimed.
findings.exactProblem: Usage roles and source values are not separately named, despite the shared spec describing tokens as semantic; theme/role changes therefore require edits to variables directly consumed throughout components.
findings.rootCause: The token vocabulary evolved incrementally in one hand-maintained stylesheet around current feature values rather than an explicit role layer.
findings.impact: Raises coupling and makes future role changes harder to audit. The present single light CSS theme remains usable; a second theme/output target is not established.
findings.currentSafePatch: No source patch is indicated or applied. Preserve current --micro-* names and rendered values while planning any aliases.
findings.futureState: Keep the current CSS file and light-only direction as the compatibility base. If approved, add a small semantic alias layer for repeated theme-dependent roles, then migrate consumers incrementally. Add border, opacity, layer, breakpoint or elevation roles only where repeated source decisions justify them. Defer DTCG/build tooling until a second output platform or explicit typed-token workflow is approved.
findings.recommendedApproach: Treat as a low-disruption structural improvement, not a High defect. Define roles and compatibility aliases first; test for cycles/unmapped aliases and preserve existing screenshot values.
findings.patchVsStructural: Structural, staged; no immediate component patch.
risks: Vague aliases can hide rather than clarify meaning.
Parallel token sources can increase drift.
Tokenizing one-off geometry creates noise.
acceptance: Each semantic alias maps to a primitive or documented literal without cycles.
Theme-dependent consumer styles use roles rather than unrelated raw values.
Current approved light screenshots remain stable.
Static checks detect unregistered global layer values and unapproved raw palette colors.

ownerDecision.question: Approve a staged semantic CSS layer now, keep the one-layer contract, or adopt DTCG/build tooling?

options.effect: Lowest migration cost; future theme changes remain coupled.
Improves role clarity while preserving current values and API.
Typed multi-target source, with tooling/governance cost not yet justified.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Add semantic CSS aliases gradually; defer DTCG until a second output target is approved.
ownerDecision.blocking: Blocks final token-governance sign-off, not isolated current UI fixes.

findings.title_ar: أدوار الطبقات العامة غير محكومة
findings.recommendationAr: عرّف أدوارًا مشتركة واختبر التركيب؛ لا تصف الأرقام الحالية كعطل تراكب مثبت.

rawMetadata.note: Confirmed governance gap only; no current overlay malfunction was proven.

findings.evidence: Global-looking values 80, 85 and 90 encode backdrop, layer and toast ordering; showcase chrome uses 60, and other values 1/2/5 are local. Current backdrops/layers/toasts have an explicit numeric ordering. Parent-reported operational overlay paths passed; there is no confirmed visual obstruction or stacking malfunction.
findings.exactProblem: Global layer roles are scattered as numeric literals without a shared explanation or stacking-context/host ownership contract.
findings.rootCause: Families and preview chrome were added incrementally without a cross-family layer-role policy.
findings.impact: Future composed overlays can be difficult to reason about, especially across stacking contexts; risk is governance/composition uncertainty, not current broken order.
findings.currentSafePatch: Do not change numbers based on this audit alone. Retain current ordering until a composition contract is approved.
findings.futureState: Define concise roles for content, sticky chrome, popover, backdrop, dialog surface and transient feedback. Document stacking-context boundaries, safe-area/viewport ownership and host override points. Keep decorative bubble stacking local. Add a composed fixture for dialog, picker, toast, sticky actionbar and navigation, including focus and close-target visibility.
findings.recommendedApproach: Structural layer roles followed by an additive CSS replacement; validate composition rather than asserting isolated numeric constants.
findings.patchVsStructural: Structural policy with later small literal replacements.
risks: A numeric scale alone cannot cross stacking contexts.
Over-prescriptive global roles constrain host composition.
Toast ordering may depend on modal ownership.
acceptance: No unexplained global overlay z-index remains.
Backdrop/layer and toast/modal order is deterministic in approved compositions.
Nested overlay fixture has no obscured close/action target at all four widths in RTL/LTR.
Focus visibility and reduced motion remain intact.

ownerDecision.question: Should toast always outrank dialogs, should the modal own the top layer, or should a host map roles?

options.effect: Confirmation remains visible but may cover dialog content/actions.

options.option: Dialog above toast (recommended default pending accessibility review)
options.effect: Protects dialog focus/context; transient feedback may wait until dialog closes.
Flexible but requires an integration contract.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Modal above toast by default, with documented host control if needed.
ownerDecision.blocking: Blocks final layer-role mapping, not current component use.

findings.title_ar: عقود دورة حياة JavaScript متفاوتة
findings.recommendationAr: وحّد اصطلاح init/update/dispose تدريجيًا مع الحفاظ على واجهات التوافق الحالية.
findings.evidence: Families expose differing combinations of init, sync, disconnect and destroy; sources also register DOM/event/observer listeners. Existing lifecycle checks passed for exercised families; this finding is the uneven public convention, not a claim of leak in every family.
findings.exactProblem: Consumers must learn family-specific initialization, idempotence, update and teardown behavior because there is no common documented convention for JS-enhanced families.
findings.rootCause: Lifecycle support was introduced incrementally as observers and interactive behavior required it.
findings.impact: Dynamic mount/removal and repeated initialization are harder to integrate consistently. Static CSS-only families do not need a lifecycle abstraction.
findings.currentSafePatch: No renaming or breaking API change now. Preserve global names and methods.
findings.futureState: Document a lightweight family-appropriate convention: idempotent init(root), explicit update/render only where data changes, and destroy/disconnect for owned observers/listeners. Document static families as no-JS-lifecycle. Test mount twice, update, detach, dispose, reattach and event count. Keep vanilla core until a host target is selected.
findings.recommendedApproach: Structural convention with additive compatibility aliases, rolled out by family and covered by shared lifecycle fixtures.
risks: A universal abstraction can hide real family differences.
Cleanup cannot necessarily restore host-owned state or focus.
Changing globals may break the current standalone contract.
acceptance: Every enhanced family documents ownership of listeners, observers, timers and generated nodes.
Repeated init is idempotent; dispose/re-init adds no duplicate behavior.
No owned observer/global listener remains after documented disposal.
Compatibility aliases remain tested through a versioned change.

ownerDecision.question: Keep the global vanilla API and standardize lifecycle, or make ESM/custom elements primary?

options.effect: No runtime/build dependency; globals remain public API.
Explicit imports/tree-shaking but requires module/build policy.
Encapsulated lifecycle with broader accessibility/style integration work.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Standardize lifecycle on the current vanilla global API until a target requires another format.
ownerDecision.blocking: Blocks final public API freeze, not existing component usage.

findings.title_ar: مدقق المخرج المستقل يتحقق من العدد لا ترتيب الاعتمادات
findings.recommendationAr: اجعل HTML أو manifest واحدًا مرجعًا، واختبر الترتيب والحذف صراحة.

rawMetadata.note: Current output itself was verified correct; weakness is checker assertion coverage.

findings.evidence: Read-only `python3 tools/build-ui-system-showcase-standalone.py --check` passed: current standalone output is byte-identical and 23 embedded icon symbols match. The builder maintains expected CSS/JS lists but checks matched link counts rather than exact ordered path equality.
findings.exactProblem: A reorder or substitution preserving the number of link tags may pass despite changed cascade/script semantics.
findings.rootCause: The dependency graph is represented in source HTML and duplicated expected arrays without an exact comparison.
findings.impact: Future dependency drift can alter standalone behavior without a path-specific failure; no current output mismatch was found.
findings.currentSafePatch: No output/source edits. Keep generated standalone untouched; current check remains a pass.
findings.futureState: Choose source HTML order or a single explicit dependency manifest as canonical. Assert exact membership and order, include assets/licenses as appropriate, and add negative tests for reorder, omission and unregistered inputs. Distinguish portable component dependencies from showcase-only chrome.
findings.recommendedApproach: Tighten exact-path validation before expanding package tooling; retain the verified output.
findings.patchVsStructural: Small checker patch plus source-of-truth clarification.
risks: Moving the duplicate catalog elsewhere may not remove drift.
A source HTML list must distinguish demo chrome from component dependencies.
acceptance: Existing standalone remains byte-identical.
Reorder/removal/unregistered-link negative tests fail with a path-specific message.
Every portable dependency is listed exactly once.
Package smoke tests do not pull showcase-only chrome.

ownerDecision.question: Should source HTML order or an explicit dependency manifest be canonical?

options.option: HTML is canonical (recommended for this vanilla library)
options.effect: Fewer sources of truth; builder validates declared order.
Supports multiple packagers but requires catalog drift tests.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Make HTML order canonical unless a second packager is approved.
ownerDecision.blocking: Does not block current UI; blocks stronger packaging-integrity sign-off.

findings.title_ar: ملخصات الحالة والفهرس قديمة ومتعارضة
findings.recommendationAr: اعتمد سجلًا واحدًا للعائلات والحالة وحدّث الإشارات التاريخية بدل فتح عيب تقويم منفصل.
findings.evidence: `components/README.md` says the library is not approved and asks to add families, while the inventory lists 14 folders with current maturity status and release docs point to that registry. `CURRENT-STATE.md` cites a different older HEAD. The calendar geometry appendix also contains dated historical measurements; those are history, not current runtime proof.
findings.exactProblem: Current-facing summaries provide conflicting library/status/revision cues and do not consistently distinguish historical measurements from current behavior.
findings.rootCause: A starter README and dated status reports coexist with newer inventory/release documentation; status and verification revision are duplicated.
findings.impact: Contributors may use stale maturity or evidence when making transfer decisions. This is documentation/governance impact only.
findings.currentSafePatch: No docs changed. After approval, correct the stale overview pointer and clearly label historical commit/geometry evidence.
findings.futureState: Create one authoritative family/status registry or explicitly name the existing inventory as source of truth. Include source/spec/example/preview links, maturity, and evidence revision. Keep dated reports but distinguish archived figures from current verified thresholds.
findings.recommendedApproach: Small documentation correction plus a lightweight consistency check; do not generate a large governance system unless useful.
risks: Automatic documentation generation may be unnecessary.
A registry must not equate library maturity with consumer-product readiness or erase history.
acceptance: No current-facing overview contradicts the family inventory.
Historical measurements/revisions are labelled as historical.
Each family has one declared maturity and source evidence link.
A read-only check detects stale hashes/status contradictions.

ownerDecision.question: None required for the minimal correction. Optional choice: patch docs only or introduce a canonical family registry.

options.option: Patch current docs and retain dated reports (recommended)
options.effect: Low effort and preserves history.

options.option: Add canonical registry and generated checks
options.effect: Less drift but adds governance/tooling.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Patch the misleading summary and clearly cross-reference historical calendar evidence.
ownerDecision.blocking: No.

findings.title_ar: MANIFEST لا يطابق الملفات المؤهلة في HEAD
findings.recommendationAr: احسم هل هو snapshot أم manifest حالي، ثم ولّد نسخة معتمدة وأضف فحصًا للقراءة فقط.

rawMetadata.note: Delivery/governance problem, not a rendered UI defect.

findings.evidence: Read-only comparison against manifest-builder eligibility rules: 434 eligible tracked files versus 286 manifest entries; 148 omitted, 66 present hashes differ, 220 match, no manifest-only paths. The manifest builder was inspected but not run because normal mode overwrites MANIFEST.json.
findings.exactProblem: If MANIFEST is intended to represent current HEAD, it is incomplete and has stale hashes; the file does not identify a frozen generation revision.
findings.rootCause: The manifest was not refreshed after source changes, or represents an undocumented frozen package snapshot.
findings.impact: Delivery consumers cannot rely on it as complete current-tree integrity evidence until its intended domain is clarified.
findings.currentSafePatch: Do not regenerate automatically. Confirm inclusion/exclusion policy first; no file was overwritten.
findings.futureState: Decide current-HEAD integrity manifest versus immutable delivery snapshot. Then regenerate or rename/document it, record revision, and add a non-writing check for missing/extra/hash-mismatched eligible files. Keep audit artifacts excluded intentionally.
findings.recommendedApproach: Owner-approved regeneration followed by read-only validation; treat as delivery gate, not a visual redesign.
risks: Blind regeneration could legitimize unintended files or expand the public package.
Inclusion policy and hidden/binary/audit exclusions need confirmation.
acceptance: Read-only validator reports zero missing/extra/hash mismatch.
Representative inclusion/exclusion rules are tested.
Validation never rewrites MANIFEST.json.

ownerDecision.question: Does MANIFEST describe current HEAD or a frozen delivery snapshot, and should eligible tracked files be its exact domain?

options.effect: Regenerate after approval and detect stale files in release checks.
Keep old hashes, label/rename the snapshot, and add separate current-source integrity data.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Current-HEAD integrity manifest after confirming policy.
ownerDecision.blocking: Blocks release-integrity sign-off; not current component or visual work.

findings.title_ar: لوحة عينات الأزرار كثيفة ومؤطرة على الهاتف
findings.recommendationAr: افصل المعاينة المختصرة عن مختبر الحالات؛ لا تصغّر الأزرار أو أهداف اللمس.
findings.category: Visual composition and density / preview information architecture
findings.evidence: At 320 CSS px, Chromium measured the first buttons specimen panel at 280×784px with 24px padding and radius. The viewed `generated-artifacts/pixilated-audit/visual-buttons-320.jpg` shows multiple examples/captions in one long rounded specimen. Sampled buttons themselves remain 48px high.
findings.exactProblem: The preview wrapper and repeated card treatment dominate mobile scanning; individual types are not organized as a compact overview versus a deep state lab.
findings.rootCause: Shared board CSS applies a 24px padded/radius panel while all examples and captions flow together.
findings.impact: Slows review of family differences on narrow screens and makes a library reference feel like nested cards. No defect in button geometry is shown.
findings.currentSafePatch: No component patch. Retain 48px targets and current component spacing; any change belongs in the review-board shell.
findings.futureState: Separate compact family overview, exhaustive state-comparison lab, and contextual composition. Use flat labeled rows on mobile, reserve surfaces for independent examples, and keep captions adjacent to their exact specimen. Move long explanation into spec links.
findings.recommendedApproach: Structural preview information-architecture/composition change, not button CSS redesign.
risks: Flattening all surfaces can make samples harder to distinguish; preserve grouping with hierarchy, section rules and spacing.
acceptance: At 320/360/390/430, sample and family labels remain visible without page overflow.
Captions map unambiguously to specimens.
Variable copy is not clipped.
A board-only change does not alter component dimensions.

ownerDecision.question: Should family previews prioritize compact inventory scanning or exhaustive state comparison?

options.effect: Fast family scan; move deep matrix to a dedicated state lab.
QA detail remains immediate but mobile page stays long.
No migration; current scan cost remains.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Compact overview first, with state lab as a separate destination.
ownerDecision.blocking: Does not block component work.

findings.title_ar: معاينة البطاقة المجاورة في Carousel شريط مقصوص
findings.recommendationAr: اجعل البطاقة المركّزة هي الافتراضية، وقدم peek اختياريًا فقط عندما يكون مقروءًا.
findings.evidence: At 430px viewport, measured sample panel 390px and carousel viewport about 342px; active card width 270px and neighboring card exposed only about 24px. Viewed `visual-carousel-430.jpg` shows a clipped sliver, while document width stays 430px; this is not page overflow.
findings.exactProblem: The adjacent-card peek exposes too little content to be a useful preview and reads like accidental clipping.
findings.rootCause: A fixed peek/gap equation is retained just above the ≤335px full-width fallback, leaving an unreadable sliver at measured 342px inner width.
findings.impact: The extra edge space consumes readable area without adding meaningful orientation; arrows, dots and position text already identify location.
findings.currentSafePatch: A threshold-only CSS patch could hide the measured sliver, but do not apply it until the default focused-vs-strip contract is decided.
findings.futureState: Make a full readable focused card the default, with explicit position and visible controls. Offer a separate browse-strip/peek mode only for short teaser-safe content at a component-inline-size threshold. Preserve swipe parity; never shrink active content to manufacture peek.
findings.recommendedApproach: Resolve the presentation API and default, then adjust the container threshold. A one-off threshold patch alone leaves the contract ambiguous.
findings.patchVsStructural: Structural variant/API decision with a bounded follow-up CSS patch.
risks: Removing peek may reduce swipe discoverability; retain visible navigation controls.
A teaser mode needs content suitable for preview.
acceptance: At component widths 288/328/342/350/390, focused mode shows no clipped neighboring copy.
Browse mode exposes a deliberate legible cue.
Active content never clips.
RTL keyboard, position announcement, one-card state and reduced motion pass.

ownerDecision.question: Is the desired default a focused active card, browse strip, or explicit variants?

options.effect: Maximizes content width and supports varied copy; peek is optional.
Promotes browsing but requires teaser-safe content and wider bounds.
Flexible but expands API and test surface.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Focused default with opt-in browse/peek.
ownerDecision.blocking: Blocks final carousel default approval.

findings.title_ar: وسوم Stable وDraft تحمل لون التحذير نفسه
findings.recommendationAr: افصل maturity عن runtime status، واستخدم حياديًا لـstable وتحذيرًا للمراجعة.
findings.evidence: Rendered boards label stable components and draft components with the same pale warning styling; `.status-chip` always uses warning surface/text tokens irrespective of maturity label. Text remains explicit, so color is not the sole signal.
findings.exactProblem: A stable implementation and a draft-for-review implementation carry the same caution cue, weakening quick maturity scanning.
findings.rootCause: One generic chip class has no explicit status-to-tone mapping.
findings.impact: Reviewers may read stability metadata as a warning. This is preview governance, not a component runtime state failure.
findings.currentSafePatch: No code changes. Confirm canonical vocabulary before styling distinct maturity roles.
findings.futureState: Define stable/reference as neutral, draft/review as restrained warning, and proposed as informational. Use explicit state classes/data attributes and keep lifecycle maturity separate from runtime error/success/warning colors.
findings.recommendedApproach: Small preview-only state mapping plus a concise maturity contract.
risks: Too many colors add noise; keep a small vocabulary and preserve text labels.
acceptance: Stable is not warning-colored.
Draft differs visibly from stable.
Proposed does not mimic runtime error.
Status remains understandable without color and actual background contrast is checked.

ownerDecision.question: Which maturity vocabulary is canonical?

options.effect: Matches current repository language and supports three tones.
Simpler but loses proposed distinction.
Flexible but weakens consistency.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Keep stable/draft/proposed.
ownerDecision.blocking: Does not block component APIs; blocks reliable status signaling.

findings.title_ar: تداخل دوائر المقارنة يحجب مساحة البيانات
findings.recommendationAr: اعتمد أشرطة أو جدولًا للدقة، واجعل الدوائر المنفصلة اختيارية والتداخل توضيحيًا فقط.

rawMetadata.note: Updated visual deep review; confirmed by measured rendered occlusion, not preference.

findings.evidence: Viewed 320px and 390px crops show 64/25/9 circles interlocking despite a no-relationship caption. At 390px diameters are 144/90/54px; measured foreground A occludes about 40.1% of B's disk and 35.6% of C's. Base diameter formula is square-root scaled, but visible areas no longer compare as 64:25:9. Exact external readings remain visible.
findings.exactProblem: The default overlap hides meaningful areas of smaller quantitative marks and creates a Venn-like relationship cue that the data do not encode; a disclaimer cannot restore the visible comparison.
findings.rootCause: The example defaults to overlap and renderer places larger circles in front at fixed relative centers to create a compact cluster.
findings.impact: Visible circle area is not proportionate to the stated 64:25:9 values even though underlying diameters are; exact labels mitigate data loss but do not make that visual encoding sound.
findings.currentSafePatch: No source change. The exact key and zero/missing/negative copy provide recovery. Do not alter area math or global data colors.
findings.futureState: Use aligned bars/list/table for precision. If area circles remain, make them disjoint, optional, and explicitly a coarse magnitude view with a meaningful shared scale and exact key. Keep overlap illustration-only or remove it from metric comparison. Preserve exact negative, zero and missing semantics.
findings.recommendedApproach: Structural/default decision for metric comparison; remove overlap from quantitative use rather than applying a cosmetic spacing tweak.
risks: Disjoint circles require a common meaningful scale.
Incomparable units should use rows rather than area marks.
Tables preserve exactness but reduce preattentive magnitude emphasis.
acceptance: Disjoint circles remain fully visible and area tracks values.
Exercise 64/25/9 with huge/zero/negative/missing cases.
Exact text remains present and negative/missing do not receive positive area.
Overlap, if retained, is non-default and explicitly illustrative.

ownerDecision.question: Keep overlap illustration-only or remove it from metric comparison?

options.effect: Preserves visible area encoding; bars/tables remain precision path.
Retains a decorative layered graphic without data-precision claim.
Compact, but occlusion and unsupported relation cues remain.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Aligned linear/table for precision; disjoint circles optional; overlap illustration-only or removed.
ownerDecision.blocking: Blocks final metric-comparison visual sign-off.

findings.title_ar: حالة Picker غير الجاهزة تُسقط التركيز من الخيار
findings.recommendationAr: انقل status إلى منطقة live مجاورة، وانقل التركيز فقط عند إخفاء العنصر المركّز.
findings.category: Asynchronous component state / keyboard focus and feedback

rawMetadata.note: Normalized upward relative to nearby polish because focus loss is dynamically reproduced in a documented API path; actual screen-reader impact remains untested.

findings.evidence: At 320/360/390/430 RTL, focus a visible role=option then call documented `MicroPicker.setStatus(picker, 'error', message)`. Options hide and Chromium moves activeElement to body. Retry remains visible and emits once. State text is inside the listbox and has no status/alert/live semantics. Browser results: 84 pass / 4 fail, with all four failures the same issue; 0 runtime errors. Viewed `interaction-360-picker-error-layer.png`.
findings.exactProblem: A focused option is removed from view without focus transfer. Loading/empty/error content and retry are inserted into the listbox rather than a status region outside its option subtree.
findings.rootCause: State transition hides options but does not relocate focus; stateRow has no live announcement role and lives in listbox semantics.
findings.impact: Keyboard continuity is directly broken for this supported async transition. Assistive-technology announcement/role confusion is plausible but not established by a real screen reader.
findings.currentSafePatch: No source change. Preserve stale-option hiding, state-specific messages, retry action and its one-event behavior.
findings.futureState: Keep listbox to options/groups; render loading/empty/error in an adjacent stable live-status region and retry outside the listbox. Move focus to a visible stable picker control only if the currently focused node is about to be hidden; never steal focus from outside or another visible control. Preserve query and still-valid selection.
findings.recommendedApproach: Targeted markup/state-transition patch, not a broad picker redesign. Polite is the default recommendation for routine states.
risks: Unconditional focus changes can interrupt users.
Too-frequent live updates can over-announce.
Screen-reader output must be manually verified before conformance claims.
acceptance: Focused option transitions leave focus on visible picker control, not body/hidden content.
Updates do not steal focus when initiated elsewhere.
Status has live semantics and listbox contains only valid options/groups.
Retry is reachable and dispatches exactly one event.
Ready recovery retains query and valid selection; repeat at four widths RTL inside a layer.

ownerDecision.question: Should async picker errors use polite status, alert, or caller-configurable urgency?

options.effect: Avoids interrupting routine/recoverable updates.
More interruptive, including background/recoverable failures.
Flexible but expands API/test surface.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Polite default; reserve alert for explicitly urgent cases.
ownerDecision.blocking: Does not block the focus repair; blocks final announcement-priority contract.

findings.title_ar: سياسة اللغة والتنسيق موزعة بين العائلات
findings.recommendationAr: احسم Arabic-only مقابل locale adapter، ثم اجمع رسائل المكوّن وصيغ الأرقام دون لمس بيانات المستهلك.

rawMetadata.note: Fragmented ownership is confirmed; no defect exists unless owner selects broader locale support.

findings.evidence: Arabic strings and generated numeric labels are embedded per component; calendar explicitly declares Arabic/Gregorian/Western digits, while other families compose text or accept caller formatting. Showcase HTML extraction found 339 unique strings but is not a complete JS/runtime catalog. This proves fragmentation, not a requirement for another language.
findings.exactProblem: No single shared policy was found for component-owned strings, date/number/plural formatting, overrides and missing keys.
findings.rootCause: Arabic-first defaults, fixture copy and consumer-owned values evolved in separate sources without a stable locale/string ownership contract.
findings.impact: Future changes may drift between visible copy, ARIA/live text, dates, digits and fixtures; no current translation failure is proven.
findings.currentSafePatch: Do not bulk-replace fixture or caller copy. No source changes.
findings.futureState: First inventory string ownership and defaults. If Arabic-only, document MSA, date, Western/Eastern digit and bidi rules centrally. If locale-ready, introduce a small adapter with stable UI-state IDs, typed interpolation, plural/date/number helpers and clear missing-key behavior. Consumer labels, units, data and business outcomes remain caller-owned; one resolved string feeds visible and accessible output.
findings.recommendedApproach: Structural content-contract decision before building infrastructure; centralize only shared state copy and formatting, avoiding a general-purpose framework without target demand.
risks: Overbuilt localization layer.
Naïve Arabic pluralization can be wrong.
Arbitrary units/business copy can be corrupted by automatic grammar.
acceptance: Approved Arabic defaults/overrides and missing-key behavior are deterministic.
Plural edge cases 0/1/2/3/10/11/99/100 tested where relevant.
Mixed Arabic/Latin identifiers and both digit families remain legible.
Visible/live string agrees and date/number formatting respects consumer-supplied displays.

ownerDecision.question: Is the kit strictly Arabic MSA or Arabic-first/locale-ready; which digit family applies to dates, metrics and entered values?

options.option: Arabic MSA and Western digits only
options.effect: Smallest API; explicitly limits locale portability.
Moderate upfront work and clearer future seam.
Most flexible with highest maintenance.

ownerDecision.recommendation: Arabic-first adapter only if locale-ready transfer is an approved goal; keep current MSA/Western defaults.
ownerDecision.blocking: Blocks shared localization contract, not unrelated visual work.

findings.title_ar: مثال 4 طلب يختلف بين النص والاسم الميسّر
findings.recommendationAr: صحح fixture المؤكد وحده؛ لا تضف pluralizer عامًا لوحدة يملكها المستهلك.
